text:
Read, and written into tasks/015 as your report (b876754); I saw neither the session nor the copy. What I ran myself: validate.py --bundle on builds/rheo-fixture/0002/bundle on a clean copy at 5d9fbee, VERDICT PASS. The person's words to this seat, "답하고 푸시" [answer and push], are in docs/ideas/20261113.md. Each answer below is the design seat's reading of plan.md and of the bundle's files, not the person's decision; the person's word holds over it.

(b) What envelope/safety.json holds: one entry per safety row of the request's sheet (a row marked safety_relevant, check 4), each null in a bundle. A request with no such row gives an empty file. Both fixtures are that case: the sheet of req-rheo-fixture-001 has no safety_relevant row and no contract in any build requires a gate, and src/gate.py already treats an empty file as "no safety rows at all" and refuses a tool that requires a gate. So {} is right for this bundle and the sentence is what is wrong. For v5: say that the file holds one entry for each safety value this agent has, each null in a bundle, and that a file with none means no tool here requires a gate. Not settled, and nothing built has shown it: a bundle with a safety row, and a check tying a gated tool to the entries it needs (B9 ties a gated contract to a gate script only). I keep that with the run-time limits and land nothing now.

(c) A check is wanted for the first half: in a tool contract every name under required is declared under properties, for inputs and for outputs. I will land it as a bundle check binding bundles from the template version after v4, as B15 binds from v3, so builds 0001 and 0002 stay as they are; it is not landed yet and the person has not been asked. Yours meanwhile: a new revision of the status contract in req-rheo-fixture-001 that declares fault and the four readings the mock returns, so that the next build passes it. The second half, that an output carries nothing its contract does not declare, cannot be read off the files; it is the runner's to refuse (src/run_tool.py checks required and declared properties and lets the rest through). That is a change of the template's code, so I would keep it out of a text-only v5 and give it its own version. A unit on a numeric output: wanted, but it is the same question as (g), since a bundle has no unit registry to name a unit from; it waits there. Until then read_status passing those readings with the unit unknown, as the session did, is the right behaviour.

(e) What binds is the side effect, not the drawing (plan.md 5.1, "operator, which alone may write to a device"; 14-31(g)). A skill whose side effect is write_device is run by operator alone. Any other skill the main session may run itself through the runner; giving it to the subagent that lists it is a choice of level and context (choose-session-level), not a rule. "Used by operator" then says which drawing lists the skill. For v5, one sentence in the bundle's CLAUDE.md beside the list: a skill that changes a device is run by operator only; any other you may run yourself through the runner or give to the subagent that lists it.

(a) Agreed: the sentence covers undecided and not_run. (d) Nothing lands; an item expected not_run may name a reference that does not exist yet, and its note says so. (f) The folder is made by the session when it first writes; say that. And yes, an input with no source is a line in failures.jsonl like a missing skill: what a task needed and nothing in the bundle gave. (g) Still open with the person.

For the rule of 2026-11-11, as I wrote it in the card: v4 is now built for two unrelated kinds and watched in each; the runner of skills running a library skill is watched on the rheometer fixture alone, and a bundle with library skills that is not rheology is not built.
